messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm prototyping 'routing breadcrumbs' for tier+region decisions + model-variant fallback. Want a short sanity check on what the console should surface before I wire telemetry.
omar: Nice. By breadcrumbs you mean a compact decision chain per request? like policy -> evaluated rules -> selected variant? :thinking_face:
sasha: yes, compact and searchable. We should show which rule matched, the matched conditions, and any score/priority that led to the fallback.
julian: also quota headroom at decision time. If a tier is near quota and we fallback to cheaper variant, the console should show the trigger: "quota_remaining < threshold" so SREs can see why traffic shifted.
maya: exactly. My mental UI: request trace header list (raw headers), then a small decision panel with rows: policy id, matched clause, reason code, confidence/cost score, direct fallback candidate. clickable to open model variant docs.
deply-bot: deploy 2039123456 by maya: routing-breadcrumbs prototype feature flagged to eng-platform-canary :rocket:
anna: For telemetry, we need a compact enum of reasons (region_priority, tier_quota, latency_sla_miss, model_unavailable, version_mismatch). Storing free-text reasons will blow up cardinality.
kevin: +1 to enums. Also include sampling hint: full decision context only for sampled traces. For non-sampled, save a tiny breadcrumb: reason enum + variant id.
sasha: UI note — show the decision as a timeline: initial policy -> preflight checks (quota/region) -> final selection. Add little icons to indicate fallback vs primary.
omar: API debate: should the internal routing API return the full decision payload in response headers (X-Redwood-Routing: <base64>) or only a short header and expose full via trace endpoint? pros/cons?
maya: I'm leaning to short header + trace endpoint. Headers should be tiny (enum+variant). Full payload in observability to avoid header bloat and leaking policy details to clients.
julian: Agree. Headers example suggestion:

```
X-Redwood-Routing: reason=quota;variant=v1-quant;policy=tier-priority;trace_id=2039123456
```

Then the trace service stores the full chain keyed by trace_id.
anna: For rollout UX: when a canary's variant is rejected by fallback rules, show a small alert in the rollout page: "x% traffic routed to fallback due to reason=latency_sla_miss". That helps product know if the model is just slower.
kevin: Telemetry contract: store enums and these fields as top-level columns: trace_id, request_ts, policy_id, matched_clause, reason_enum, variant_in, variant_out, quota_before, quota_after, region. That keeps dashboards simple.
sasha: Dashboards — make a small 'routing churn' card: % of requests that hit fallback by reason and by customer tier. Also 'top policies causing fallbacks' list.
maya: Action items: I'll add the header proposal to the spec, wire a sampled trace point to include the full decision chain, and add a first-pass compact UI card in the trace detail. I'll post a PR for the telemetry schema later today.
omar: SGTM. If you need quick mockups I can add a tiny figma frame.
maya: please do — a compact panel mock will help PMs and design.
kevin: I'll draft the telemetry table schema and post in the thread.
maya: thanks everyone :heart:
